title: Quality of science and reporting of radiomics in oncologic studies: room for improvement according to radiomics quality score and TRIPOD statement

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Quality of science and reporting of radiomics in oncologic studies: room for improvement according to radiomics quality score and TRIPOD statement》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Objectives · abstract-1-1】To evaluate radiomics studies according to radiomics quality score (RQS) and Transparent Reporting of a multivariable prediction model for Individual Prognosis Or Diagnosis (TRIPOD) to provide objective measurement of radiomics research.

【Results · abstract-3-1】Seventy-seven articles were included. The mean RQS score was 26.1% of the maximum (9.4 out of 36). The RQS was low in demonstration of clinical utility (19.5%), test-retest analysis (6.5%), prospective study (3.9%), and open science (3.9%). None of the studies conducted a phantom or cost-effectiveness analysis. The adherence rate for TRIPOD was 57.8% (mean) and was particularly low in reporting title (2.6%), stating study objective in abstract and introduction (7.8% and 16.9%), blind assessment of outcome (14.3%), sample size (6.5%), and missing data (11.7%) categories. Studies in clinical journals scored higher and more frequently adopted external validation than imaging journals.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Quality of science and reporting of radiomics in oncologic studies: room for improvement according to radiomics quality score and TRIPOD statement》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Materials and methods · abstract-2-1】PubMed and Embase were searched for studies published in high clinical imaging journals until December 2018 using the terms "radiomics" and "radiogenomics." Studies were scored against the items in the RQS and TRIPOD guidelines. Subgroup analyses were performed for journal type (clinical vs. imaging), intended use (diagnostic vs. prognostic), and imaging modality (CT vs. MRI), and articles were compared using Fisher's exact test and Mann-Whitney analysis.

【Results · abstract-3-1】Seventy-seven articles were included. The mean RQS score was 26.1% of the maximum (9.4 out of 36). None of the studies conducted a phantom or cost-effectiveness analysis. sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Quality of science and reporting of radiomics in oncologic studies: room for improvement according to radiomics quality score and TRIPOD statement》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · abstract-3-1】Seventy-seven articles were included. The mean RQS score was 26.1% of the maximum (9.4 out of 36). The RQS was low in demonstration of clinical utility (19.5%), test-retest analysis (6.5%), prospective study (3.9%), and open science (3.9%). Studies in clinical journals scored higher and more frequently adopted external validation than imaging journals.

【Conclusions · abstract-4-1】The overall scientific quality and reporting of radiomics studies is insufficient. Scientific improvements need to be made to feature reproducibility, analysis of clinical utility, and open science categories. Reporting of study objectives, blind assessment, sample size, and missing data is deemed to be necessary.
